item.title: The Sonoma County Fair — Mon Aug 10, 10:00 AM — Sonoma County Fairgrounds
item.description:
A celebration of community spirit, agriculture, entertainment, and wholesome fun.
The Sonoma County Fair is an annual event that captivates visitors with its vibrant atmosphere and diverse offerings. Held in scenic Sonoma County, California, this fair is a celebration of community spirit, agriculture, entertainment, and wholesome fun. From thrilling amusement rides and live music performances to engaging exhibits showcasing local produce, crafts, and artwork, the fair offers something for everyone. Attendees can indulge in mouthwatering fair food, participate in thrilling competitions, enjoy live animal exhibits, and explore the region’s rich agricultural heritage. With its charming blend of entertainment and education, the Sonoma County Fair is a must-visit destination that brings joy and excitement to people of all ages.
Source: GoLocal Cooperative

item.title: Gypsy Trio at Furthermore Wines (Healdsburg) — Tue Aug 11, 5:30 PM — Furthermore Wines
item.description:
The Gypsy Trio plays music in the spirit of early 20th-century Parisian music à la Django Reinhardt. The band consists of some of the best musicians the area has to offer. Guitarits: Ian Scherer, Emily Froberg, and bassist Trevor Kinsel. The Chemistry of The Gypsy Trio is greater than the sum of its parts. The two guitars "weave" back and forth switching between lead and rhythm guitar and, at times,play the same part, but always in perfect juxtaposed harmony; the bass alone holds down the bottom rhythm.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.title: Art in the Redwoods Festival at Gualala Arts — Fri Aug 14, 12:00 AM — Gualala Arts Center
item.description:
Art in the Redwoods celebrates its 65th anniversary August 14–17 with a vibrant weekend of fine art, local artists, live music, food, drinks, and family-friendly entertainment. The festivities begin with the Hats Off in the Garden Dinner on August 14, followed by a Champagne Preview on August 15 featuring an early look at the fine art exhibition and outdoor artist booths. Festival days on August 16 and 17 offer guests the chance to explore juried artwork, shop from local artists, enjoy live performances, and take part in family activities, including crafts and storytelling. Additional highlights include food and beverages, tie-dye activities, and a Sunday raffle drawing and Most Popular Artwork announcement. Advance festival and Champagne Preview tickets are available at the Dolphin, with admission for children 17 and under free with a paying adult.
Source: Press Democrat

item.title: Nervous System Reset: A Nature-Based Coaching Experience #2 — Sat Aug 15, 9:30 AM — Lagoon Valley/Pena Adobe Regional Park
item.description:
We will meet by the lake near the playground, past the dog park and parking lot. 90 minutes of movement, reflection, and meaningful connection in nature. Who This is For: Exhausted women and thoughtful humans who want space to slow down, clear their mind, and reconnect with themselves away from the noise, pressure, and constant doing. Join us for a gentle guided walk in nature paired with reflective coaching prompts, mindful conversation, and quiet moments to breathe, notice, and reset. You’ll leave feeling: → more grounded → mentally clearer → emotionally lighter → connected to yourself and others → renewed for the week ahead No hiking experience needed. Just comfortable shoes, a hat/sunglasses, water, and an open heart. Come as you are. Leave feeling more like yourself.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Opening Reception: Visions of the Living Earth — Sat Aug 15, 5:00 PM — Usher Gallery
item.description:
Contemporary Australian artist Tracy Marie Shapland is reflecting her ongoing exploration of the world through color, intuition, and imagination. Inspired by her experiences of travel, nature, music and human connection, Tracy Marie begins each painting with a feeling rather than a fixed plan. Now, she’s bringing that feeling to Petaluma.
Opening on Tuesday, August 11th, 2026 at Usher Gallery (located at 1 Petaluma Blvd North), her showcase, "VISIONS OF THE LIVING EARTH: where the land remembers us" fuses botanical subjects, wildlife, waterways, abstract landscapes and imagined environments while being influenced by the diverse environment of Australia and Northern California. The exhibition will run through Sunday, September 6th, 2026.
The public is invited to a celebratory Opening Reception on Saturday, August 15, 2026, from 5:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at the gallery. The evening will feature fine wine, local refreshments, live music by the Loralee Christensen Combo and a chance to meet

item.title: Our California Group Art Show — Sat Aug 15, 6:00 PM — Laguna Lab
item.description:
THE SONOMA 5 is a freeform Northern California artist collective united by a shared interest in contemporary fine art, storytelling, and the enduring power of creative community. For OUR CALIFORNIA at Laguna Lab, the group will explore the altered and unalterable states of mind, body, and spirit that the great State of California evokes. Come engage with a stylistically diverse group of painters and assemblage artists whose voices range from the playful to the profound, unbound by any particular “ism.” Omar Mueller Jane Manning Walt Morton Tamsin Smith Josef Szuecs Bill Krinard Adam Wolpert
Source: Sebastopol Calendar

item.title: Julio Bravo y su Orquesta Salsabor — Sun Aug 16, 1:00 PM — Vino Godfather
item.description:
Celebrating their 30th anniversary, Julio Bravo's group of dynamic musicians have created a flavor all their own. Beyond the talent of each individual member, Julio Bravo y su Orquesta Salsabor, is a unique blend of vocal styles unlike other salsa bands in San Francisco. Peruvian born singer, composer, and bandleader, Julio Bravo creates an explosion of sound and energy that keeps their diverse audience coming back for more.
Julio Bravo y su Orquesta Salsabor brings together the most talented and ambitious musicians, and creates a fantastic orchestra, that has demonstrated to be energetic, versatile, fun to watch, fun to dance to, and works well in gala and outdoor events, universities, weddings, night clubs, casinos, conventions, and more, showcasing an eclectic mix of the best danceable tunes, covers and originals, they play songs ranging from their CDs "10 Anos de Salsa" & "Bravissimo" to current artists such as El Gran Combo, Gilberto Santa Rosa, Puerto Rican Power and many more.

item.title: John Moore Film Screening — Sat Aug 29, 3:30 PM — Unitarian Universalist Fellowship of North Bay
item.description:
On August 27th, 1905, John Moore, from Dover, NC, was lynched after an accusation of assaulting a white woman in Clarks, NC on August 25th. Moore was soon captured and brought to court for a hearing in New Bern, NC. After being arraigned, the following day, at approximately 1 am on the morning on of August 27th, Moore was abducted by a group of masked white men and taken to the Neuse River Bridge, located downtown New Bern, where he was hung and shot in an act of racial violence. Join the “Forward Together” coalition for a 10-minute film screening on John Moore by filmmaker Francine Robinson. The project is supported by the Equal Justice Initiative as part of their Community Remembrance Projects. For more information on the Forward Together coalition and John Moore, visit cravenarts.org/eji.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

The event is designed to introduce you to bocce ball, to try something new, to just enjoy and not be critical of yourself... just have fun! You are welcome to bring food to share with others. I will bring some cheese/charcuterie items to share.

item.title: History Talk: Cnopius Field - Sebastopol's First Airfield (1925-1942) — Sun Aug 30, 2:00 PM — Sebastopol Center for the Arts
item.description:
Did you know that in 1925, Sebastopol had its own nationally recognized airfield? Learn about this piece of unique history at a free talk at the Sebastopol Center for the Arts on Sunday, August 30th. The airfield was the first in Sonoma County, long before the Charles M. Schultz-Sonoma County Airport. It played a major role in the barnstorming era of the 1910s-1930s and was a lively hub for early aviation events, stunt flying, and community gatherings. Gary Greenough will share the colorful and fascinating history of when Sebastopol was a flying hub. This 1-hour talk is a project from the Western Sonoma County Historical Society. It will be preceded by a short update by the society board about what is happening at the Historical Society, Luther Burbank Experiment Farm, and West County Museum. The event is free and open to the public.
Source: North Bay Bohemian
